sections.heading: IS COOKING IRUMA'S FORTE?
sections.content:
Q: After finishing The Circumstances of 660 Yen,[ref:660yen-book] I have to ask — what's Iruma-sensei's specialty dish? I can make yakisoba (the Nissin instant kind) and fried rice; I'm still practicing pork cutlet rice.

A: I can't cook anything at all, so I think people who can cook are amazing. Keep practicing!

sections.heading: HOW THE WRITING ACTUALLY HAPPENS
sections.content:
Q: I read From the Bottom of Europa — the content and characters were as fun as ever. Will this one get a continuation? Also, every time I read your books, I want to ask: how do you come up with the phrasing in your descriptions and narration? Does it come from banging your head against a pillow or the corner of your computer? And do your stories come to you suddenly, or do you follow some kind of method? If it's the latter, what's the method? If it's the former, does it feel like glimpsing something you'll write in the future?

A: Whether From the Bottom of Europa gets a continuation or not — the book itself already has that kind of open-ended feeling, so I think it's fine as is. As for descriptions, if I can't think of anything, I just write more. If a phrase sounds cool, I use it. As for the story itself, I add to it and think it through as I go. Lately what I enjoy doing is scrapping everything I've already written and rewriting it as a completely different story. It's a real headache.

sections.heading: IS THE PROTAGONIST BASED ON HIMSELF?
sections.content:
Q: I finished From the Bottom of Europa — the opening, showing the protagonist's daily life as a writer, felt incredibly authentic… is that based on Iruma-sensei's own experience?

A: This work is unrelated to any real persons or organizations.

sections.heading: ARGUING FOR "USELESS" TIME
sections.content:
Q: I'm a high schooler currently studying for exams. It's spring break, but my teachers keep saying to cut down on time spent on things outside of studying — reading novels, manga, watching anime, napping, and so on. I don't think that kind of time (or really any time in life) is actually useless, but I can't think of a good counterargument. Next time I hear that line, I want to silently push back in my head and put on a smug little smile — please help me come up with something, Iruma-sensei.

A: There's no such thing as "useless" — that fact alone is a sufficient rebuttal. But your teachers were once high schoolers just like you, and after living through that stage of life, they still ended up saying something that harsh to a high schooler like you. Maybe there's something worth thinking about in that.

sections.heading: ARE THE WRITER CHARACTERS REALLY HIM?
sections.content:
Q: With works about writers, like The Naked Idiot Comes Running and From the Bottom of Europa, I feel like the fictional novels those protagonists publish resemble your own actual work. Is that because you're drawing on your own feelings and current circumstances in those stories?

A: Those are all pure fiction, and I think that's for the best.

sections.heading: STILL WAITING ON N743327 AND LZEEHLN
sections.content:
Q: Still no continuation for N743327 and LZEEHLN? I really want to know what happens next!

A: I'm planning to buckle down on those starting next year… sorry for making you wait so long.

sections.heading: LIVING SITUATION AND CURRY SPICE LEVEL
sections.content:
Q: I don't know if I'm allowed to ask this… does Iruma-sensei live alone? Also, do you like your curry mild, medium, hot, or extra-hot?

A: I've always lived with my family. I can't eat anything but mild curry. At a signing event two years ago, I ate spicy curry, and even though I acted totally fine in front of fans, I couldn't handle it once it was over. I wonder if any of them noticed.

sections.heading: LEARNING THE YURI GENRE
sections.content:
Q: In the afterword to Adachi and Shimamura, you mentioned referencing "Yuru○○○" (Note: Yuru Yuri) — do you have any other yuri manga or novels you like?[ref:yuruyuri]

A: I don't know this genre very well… if you know any good ones, please tell me. I need to study up, or I'll run into trouble writing.

sections.heading: HOW MUCH DOES A BOOK ACTUALLY EARN HIM?
sections.content:
Q: Roughly how much income does buying one of your books contribute to you?

A: It depends on the book's price, but on average, probably around five Umaibou sticks' worth.[ref:umaibou]

sections.heading: SAVING THE WORLD WITH FISH CAKE
sections.content:
Q: If you had to save the world, which would be more useful — a fried egg or fish cake? For the record, I'm on team radish.

A: I prefer fish cake. Fried eggs are fine too, but I can't really handle a runny yolk.

sections.heading: WHY MEDIAWORKS BUNKO FITS HIS STYLE
sections.content:
Q: Lately it seems like you're publishing fewer books through Dengeki Bunko than MediaWorks Bunko — do you find short stories more enjoyable to write? Personally, I like both… Also, any plans to write another "short story that feels like a long one," published outside the bunko format, like My Small-Scale Miracle?

A: I think the number of books each publisher puts out this year will probably end up about the same… My work generally doesn't have big action set pieces, isekai settings, or flashy trump-card moments, so it might just be a better fit for MediaWorks Bunko. I've never actually been to a café, so I guess I'm still young at heart! As for a "long-form" work, do you mean a hardcover? Once MediaWorks Bunko was established, there was no longer a need to specifically publish hardcovers, since those end up more expensive.[ref:mediaworks-bunko]

sections.heading: WHAT IS PAPICO?
sections.content:
Q: Do you like Papico (an ice cream product made by Ezaki Glico)?

A: I had no idea what that was — I looked it up and found out it's an ice cream. I thought it was some kind of cookie snack. I'll try it next time.

sections.heading: MAKING A PART-TIME JOB BEARABLE
sections.content:
Q: Is there some magic phrase that makes a part-time job fun?

A: It's not really possible to actually start liking work… I think what matters is knowing clearly why you're working the job, and always keeping that goal in mind. I've never actually held a job myself, but I still think that's important.

sections.heading: MAKING YOUR STORY UNDERSTANDABLE
sections.content:
Q: When a story has already taken shape in my head and I want to turn it into a novel (or in my case, a manga), how do I make it easier for readers to understand? Since I already have the full story in my head, I can follow along even with insufficient explanation or description of events — but readers might find it confusing or uncomfortable. Also, aren't high schoolers romantic prospects to you? Or do you think, "what's this kid who doesn't even know how to put on makeup talking about"?

A: This might sound contradictory, but having someone else actually read what you've written is the best approach. Getting them to point out what's hard to follow is the most practical method. For creative questions like this, you could try sending them to the Dengeki Bunko radio show (though I'm not sure if it's still running). As for high schoolers — don't high schoolers wear makeup nowadays? I imagine even middle schoolers might be doing it these days.

sections.heading: RECHARGING CREATIVITY WITH BACK TO THE FUTURE
sections.content:
Q: What do you do when you're out of inspiration?

A: When I've got no inspiration, I binge-watch the entire Back to the Future trilogy in one sitting, which makes me feel like I absolutely have to write something. In my downtime, I entertain myself by imitating lines like "Soil, my power!"[ref:ffu-quote] The subtitle of my most recent work was also inspired by this — I don't know how many people actually noticed, though.

sections.heading: A REVOLVING-DOOR NIGHT OWL
sections.content:
Q: I've heard most writers are night owls — is Iruma-sensei one too? Or are you more of a morning or daytime person?

A: When I'm not that busy, I try to go to bed early, but before I know it, I've turned back into a night owl… it's a constant back-and-forth. Not being busy comes with its own troubles too.

sections.heading: THE NAME BEHIND FUBUKI
sections.content:
Q: Does the name "Fūyuki" (a term appearing in The Fluffy Girl Falls from the Sky) come from combining the "wind" of "flowers, birds, wind, and moon" with the "snow" of "snow, moon, and flowers"?

A: There's a science fiction novel called Battle Fairy Yukikaze…[ref:yukikaze]

sections.heading: FAVORITE CHARACTER DESIGNS
sections.content:
Q: Please tell me your favorite characters, going by their illustrated designs. Name a few if you can — my favorites are Tamako and Ellio.

A: Going purely by appearance in the artwork, I like Ooe Yuna and Namekuji. I'm also fond of the chibi versions on the back covers of Electric Girl and Adolescent Boy and The Lizard King.

sections.heading: WILL SHA EVER GET HER OWN STORY?
sections.content:
Q: Hoshinaka Sha from Electric Girl and Adolescent Boy has always been such a mystery. Do you have any plans to write a story with Sha as the protagonist?

A: She was always meant to be a character shrouded in mystery, so I doubt there'll be any plans like that.

sections.heading: A DIET OF FLOUR
sections.content:
Q: What do you eat often, or what's your favorite food?

A: Takoyaki, okonomiyaki… now that I think about it, it's all flour-based food.

sections.heading: WHY BECOME A NOVELIST?
sections.content:
Q: The protagonist of From the Bottom of Europa becomes a novelist because he has nothing else he can do. So why did Iruma Hitoma-sensei want to become a novelist? If there was a specific trigger, please share that too.

A: Because there was nothing else I could do!

sections.heading: A SURPRISE DETECTIVE CONAN CAMEO
sections.content:
Q: I just saw that shrunken-detective special feature at the bookstore (Note: referring to the Detective Conan feature in the May 2014 issue of the magazine Da Vinci), and there was commentary from Iruma-kuma[ref:iruma-bear] in there. For some reason it made me both excited and moved ヾ(´・∀・)ノ. Iruma-kuma, do you prefer the anime or the manga version of this series?

A: Ah, that — while I'm honored, I still don't really understand why they came to me. When I actually saw the finished piece in print, I worried whether I stuck out awkwardly. There must have been more fitting people they could've asked! It felt like... that kind of feeling. By the way, I mostly read the Conan manga, and only occasionally watch the anime, since I don't really have a habit of watching TV.[ref:conan-davinci]

sections.heading: VOLUME 3, HOPEFULLY EARLY NEXT YEAR
sections.content:
Q: My favorites are the Detective Hanasaki Tarou series and the Six Guns, Six People, Six Days series! Every time I read the back-and-forth banter between Kisogawa-san and Hanasaki-san, I just roll around laughing! So, roughly when will Six Guns, Six People, Six Days come out?

A: Next year… sorry, I'll do my best to get Volume 3 out as early as possible next year.

sections.heading: IS THIS FAN FICTION OR SOMETHING ELSE?
sections.content:
Q: The story I wrote accidentally ended up resembling senior Iruma's work. It's a novel where the protagonist is named Asa-kun and the heroine is named Ko-chan (though she's rarely called that). Even though the content is different, and the protagonist doesn't like lying either, does this count as a derivative work? I'm not sure — should I look up senior Iruma's home address and mail it there? If confidence is what a writer needs, should I just submit it to Dengeki myself in person? I'm lost.

A: Why not just finish writing it and submit it as-is? I don't think you need to worry too much about the names.

sections.heading: SEVENTEEN AND ARMED WITH A METAL BAT
sections.content:
Q: Iruma-sensei, I'd love to read a story starring Akkyun and Ma-chan's daughter. Please write it.

A: I'm actually considering writing something like that, so please don't get your hopes up too high and just wait patiently. Right now the plan basically only amounts to "a seventeen-year-old high school girl swinging a metal bat around."

sections.heading: NO SEQUEL FOR FUWAFUWA
sections.content:
Q: Will The Fluffy Girl Falls from the Sky get a sequel?

A: I really did think through a lot of the setting details, but it seems like this book's being treated as a one-and-done, so who knows how that'll go.

sections.heading: TRAINING LIKE DRAGONFLY
sections.content:
Q: I love Dragonfly from The Lizard King — how can I learn to swing an aluminum-alloy case around as freely as he does? Dragonfly is an angel.

A: Go build up your body at the gym, and then you too can breathe in chlorine at the pool. But that's dangerous, so please don't actually try any of this.

sections.heading: A FAVORITE YURI PAIRING
sections.content:
Q: Reading Adachi and Shimamura, I got hit right in the moe spot and ended up screaming and rolling on the floor lol. Please tell me Iruma-sensei's favorite yuri couple.

A: I'm not too familiar with this area, but in Yuru○○○, I like the pairing of Sakurako and Himawari.[ref:yuruyuri]

sections.heading: NOT SHARING HIS ADDRESS
sections.content:
Q: Every time I pass through Kisogawa, I think, "could Iruma Hitoma be around here?" and look around for a man wearing a kimono, but I never find one. Could you tell me your address?

A: I can't just casually hand out my personal information. You should be careful too!

sections.heading: MORE SCREEN TIME FOR YAMAZAKI
sections.content:
Q: Will there be a Mugen Loop Game 3? Personally, I'd love more screen time for Yamazaki (lol). I'm really looking forward to the continuation, and I'm rooting for you!

A: Yamazaki gets quite a lot of screen time in Route A. As for Route B — well, given everything, you know how it is.

sections.heading: A BOOK WRITTEN BY A FRIEND?
sections.content:
Q: Sensei, sensei. What is Makai Detective Meiousei O? (lol) That's a book you wrote back before you went by "Iruma Hitoma," right? (lol)

A: That was written by my friend, Echizen Matarou.[ref:echizen-mataro] In particular, the book WALKING no W is fantastic — it really deserves high praise.

sections.heading: NAMING ELLIOTT AND JOJO'S DAUGHTER
sections.content:
Q: What's the name of Elliott and Jojo's daughter, who appears in the web short story?

A: Not decided yet. If "E.T." ever gets a sequel, everyone will find out.

sections.heading: FUSHIMI'S BIRTHDAY, SORT OF
sections.content:
Q: Is the birthday of Fushimi, the busty beauty heroine of Liar, Broken, January 15th? It has to be. Please say yes, Iruma-kuma.

A: What day is that supposed to be? Strawberry Day?[ref:strawberry-day] Not, like, Breast Day, right? Well, sure, let's just go with that.

sections.heading: A NAME MASHUP FROM OUR SEVEN-DAY WAR
sections.content:
Q: Congratulations on the release of Desert Boys' Life! Are the protagonists' names "Aichi" and "Kikuhara" a blend of two character names from Osamu Souda's Our Series (Note: referring to the two protagonists of Souda's Our Seven-Day War, Kikuchi Eiji and Aihara Toru)? Or am I reading too much into it?[ref:bokura-nanokakan]

A: That's exactly right. I read that series back in middle and high school, and it left a deep impression on me.

sections.heading: WHAT HIGH SCHOOL TAKES FROM YOU
sections.content:
Q: So, I've become a high schooler now. Sensei, did you lose anything when you became a high schooler?

A: I lost my youth. And in exchange, I gained a fool's worth of experience in high school. High school is, in a certain sense, the peak of life, so please enjoy it fully.

sections.heading: IS THERE A GIRL IN DISGUISE?
sections.content:
Q: The "beautiful girl" quota in "Mirage" (a chapter of Desert Boys' Life) seems pretty thin — does that mean Aichi cross-dresses?

A: Nakaguchi (the only female character in Desert Boys' Life) doesn't seem all that likely to be regarded as a beautiful girl, in pretty much every sense of the word.

sections.heading: CONSISTENCY OVER EVERYTHING
sections.content:
Q: What's essential for a writer? Also, do you feel you've been influenced by anyone? Or that you've influenced anyone else?

A: Sticking with the work consistently is key. I think that's true for any job. Since there's no "Iruma Hitoma II" or "Iruma Hitoma Jr." out there yet, I don't think I've influenced anyone else so far.

sections.heading: IS SHIMAMURA HŌGETSU A REAL NAME?
sections.content:
Q: Is "Shimamura Hōgetsu" from Adachi and Shimamura her actual real name?

A: For the time being, yes.[ref:shimamura-hougetsu]

sections.heading: NEVER HELD A JOB
sections.content:
Q: Iruma-sensei, did you have any part-time jobs during your student days?

A: I've never held a part-time job in my life. If it were possible, I'd want to live a life where I never have to leave the house for work.

sections.heading: SHIMAMURA'S RELATIONSHIP WITH LONELINESS
sections.content:
Q: I have a question about Adachi and Shimamura. Shimamura seems indifferent to and undemanding of pretty much everyone — is that because she has a little sister who opens up only to her, so she doesn't feel lonely even without friends?

A: Hmm, that's not something I'd thought through very deeply before. It's possible her attitude toward relationships in general is just that she finds them troublesome.

sections.heading: HOW LONG SHOULD A NOVEL BE?
sections.content:
Q: I'm currently working hard to become a writer and writing all kinds of things. It suddenly occurred to me — does a full-length novel need to be several hundred pages of manuscript paper? The most I've ever written is a bit over a hundred pages, and I want to know how to write more.

A: Manuscript paper sizes vary, so it's hard for me to give you a specific page count. But you don't need to force yourself to write a lot. What matters most is finding the length that actually suits the story. Too long or too short can both be… ah, did I say something wrong there? Questions like this should go to (as previously mentioned, et cetera).

sections.heading: NO FRIENDS TO BASE CHARACTERS ON
sections.content:
Q: Are any of the characters in your work based on your own friends?

A: I don't have any friends…

sections.heading: A CONTINUITY SLIP, NOT A CLUE
sections.content:
Q: I really love Adachi and Shimamura. So, who actually got to the second floor of the gymnasium first? The two of them seem to remember it differently — is that some kind of intentional foreshadowing?

A: Sorry, that was honestly just a mistake on my part. Ha ha ha… I'm really sorry about that.

sections.heading: A NEW ELECTRIC GIRL SHORT STORY, SOON
sections.content:
Q: Could you write a short story for Electric Girl and Adolescent Boy on the website?

A: I'll write one sometime soon.

references.title: The Circumstances of 660 Yen
references.note: Rokuhyaku Rokujūen no Jijō ("The Circumstances of 660 Yen") is a real MediaWorks Bunko novel by Iruma Hitoma, published in May 2010.

references.title: Yuru Yuri, and the Sakurako/Himawari Pairing
references.note: Yuru Yuri is a long-running four-panel yuri manga and anime series by Namori. Sakurako Ōmuro and Himawari Furuya, childhood friends who bicker constantly while clearly caring for each other, form one of the series' most popular pairings, commonly nicknamed "Hima-Saku" by fans.

references.title: Umaibou
references.note: Umaibou is an extremely cheap, iconic Japanese corn-puff snack stick made by Yaokin, first sold in 1979. At the time of this Q&A its price had held steady at 10 yen per stick since launch (it wasn't raised until 2022, and again in 2024), making Iruma's joke a real (if very small) dollar amount — about 50 yen, or roughly what a very inexpensive royalty cut might look like.

references.title: Hardcover vs. Bunko Publishing
references.note: Japanese publishing commonly distinguishes between hardcover (tankōbon) editions and the smaller, cheaper, standardized bunko paperback format that most light novels use. Iruma's more literary works, My Small-Scale Miracle and The Isolated, were originally released as non-bunko hardcovers before later being reissued as bunko editions once Kadokawa's MediaWorks Bunko imprint — aimed at exactly this kind of literary-leaning fiction — was established.

references.title: "Soil, My Power!"
references.note: "Soil, waga chikara!" ("Soil, my power!") is the catchphrase of Kuroki Kaze ("Black Wind"), the near-silent protagonist of the anime FF:U ~Final Fantasy: Unlimited~, said whenever he activates the transforming weapon fused to his arm.

references.title: Battle Fairy Yukikaze
references.note: Sentō Yōsei Yukikaze ("Battle Fairy Yukikaze") is a long-running science fiction novel series by Chōhei Kanbayashi, following a sentient reconnaissance fighter jet named Yukikaze and its human pilot. It also received a 2002 OVA adaptation.

references.title: "Iruma-kuma"
references.note: "Iruma-kuma" ("Iruma Bear") appears to be an affectionate nickname fans use for Iruma Hitoma, playing off the visual resemblance between the characters for "Iruma" and the word for "bear" (kuma), or simply as a cutesy diminutive; the questioner and Iruma both use it here.

references.title: The Detective Conan Feature in Da Vinci
references.note: The reference is to a Detective Conan retrospective feature that ran in the May 2014 issue of Da Vinci, a Japanese book-culture magazine, which included short guest commentary from a number of contributors, apparently including Iruma.

references.title: Echizen Matarou
references.note: Echizen Matarou is a shared pen name used collectively by eight authors — including Iruma Hitoma, Otaro Maijo, Ao Omine, Yoshinobu Akita, Otsuichi, Eiji Mikage, and others — for a collaborative multi-author series, Makai Tantei Meiōsei O, published in May 2010. Iruma's answer plays along with the bit that this was a separate, real "friend."

references.title: "Strawberry Day" (January 15th)
references.note: In Japan, January 15th is informally associated with strawberries via a numeral wordplay: "1" and "5" can be read as "i" and "go," combining to sound like ichigo, the Japanese word for strawberry.

references.title: Our Seven-Day War
references.note: Bokura no Nanokakan Sensō ("Our Seven-Day War") is a 1985 novel by Osamu Souda, the first entry in his long-running "Bokura" series, about a group of middle schoolers who barricade themselves in an abandoned factory in defiance of the adults around them. Its two central characters are Kikuchi Eiji and Aihara Tōru — the basis for the blended character names "Kikuhara" and "Aichi" in Iruma's Desert Boys' Life.

references.title: Shimamura Hōgetsu
references.note: Shimamura Hōgetsu is also the name of a real early-20th-century Japanese literary critic, novelist, and theater reformer, best known for his relationship with actress Sumako Matsui and his role in modernizing Japanese theater. Iruma's own character shares the name.
